seo.title: Apple Business Showcases: Promote Offers on Maps
seo.meta_description: How to create Apple Business showcases that promote offers, events and new items on your Apple Maps place card, with limits and review times, for OC businesses.

h1: Apple Business Showcases: Promote Offers and Events on Apple Maps
answer: Apple Business showcases are modules on your Apple Maps place card that highlight new items, deals, events or other promotions, with a headline, short text, an image and a call-to-action button. Apple reviews each one, so plan at least three days ahead. Showcases run up to 365 days, 90 by default. Anaheim and Orange County businesses can use them like a storefront window on Maps.
key_takeaways: Showcases appear on the place card.
Headline up to 38 characters; body up to 100.
Each one is reviewed by Apple.
Plan at least three calendar days ahead.

sections.heading: Apple Business Connect is now Apple Business
sections.body_html: Apple's guide states that Apple Business Connect is now Apple Business, which combines what was previously in Apple Business Manager, Apple Business Essentials and Apple Business Connect into one offering. If you used Apple Business Connect before, you can sign in to Apple Business with the same personal Apple Account.

sections.heading: What a showcase is
sections.body_html: Apple's guide describes a showcase as a module on the place card that highlights new items, deals or sales, or other promotional content, with a call to action. Showcases are specific to a location and a time period, and you can create them yourself or have a partner create them.

sections.heading: What goes in a showcase
sections.body_html:
• A headline of up to 38 characters.
  • A body of up to 100 characters describing the offer or event.
  • An image, at least 492 x 492 pixels and square.
  • A call-to-action button that can link to a specific opportunity.

sections.heading: How long showcases run
sections.body_html: Apple says showcases can run for up to 365 days, with a default of 90 days. Apple designed them to highlight something new, so customers keep coming back.

sections.heading: Plan ahead
sections.body_html: Because Apple reviews each showcase, it recommends planning at least three calendar days before you want one to go live, and notes that editing a showcase while it's in review may delay approval.

sections.heading: How to create one
sections.body_html:
1. In Apple Business, choose Brands, Locations and select the location.
  2. Select Showcases, then Create.
  3. Add a photo from the Asset Gallery or upload one, with alt text up to 100 characters.
  4. Add the heading, body and action.
  5. Add other languages if needed, then submit.

sections.heading: Multiple locations
sections.body_html: Apple says you can use the same showcase for every location or different ones, depending on your strategy. A brand with stores in Anaheim, Irvine and Costa Mesa could run one company-wide offer and a local event at a single store.

sections.heading: Languages
sections.body_html: Apple notes that not all languages are supported for showcases, and you can add headings and body text in each supported language you want to appear.

sections.heading: Ideas for local businesses
sections.body_html:
• A seasonal menu or new product.
  • A holiday sale or limited-time offer.
  • An in-store event or class.
  • A new service launch.
  • A booking promotion for a quiet period.

sections.heading: Showcases and Google posts
sections.body_html: Showcases do on Apple Maps what Google Business Profile posts and offers do on Google. Run the same promotion on both, adjusted for each platform's limits.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
sections.body_html:
• Submitting the day before an event.
  • Editing during review.
  • Headlines over 38 characters.
  • Images that aren't square.
  • Leaving expired offers live.

sections.heading: Questions owners ask us
sections.body_html: Owners often ask how often to update showcases. Apple recommends planning so customers always see something new each month, so a monthly rhythm works well for most local businesses: a new item, a seasonal offer, an event. Another common question is what makes a good headline in 38 characters. Lead with the benefit and the specific item, such as Fall menu: pumpkin bread is back, rather than a generic welcome. Owners also ask whether showcases need a discount. They don't; new items, events and announcements work too. Keep a simple calendar of showcases alongside your Google posts and email newsletter so promotions stay consistent across channels.

sections.heading: Checklist
sections.body_html:
• Square image at least 492 x 492.
  • Headline under 38 characters.
  • Body under 100 characters.
  • Action linked.
  • Submitted three days ahead.
  • Monthly calendar planned.

sections.heading: An example
sections.body_html: Imagine a coffee shop in Costa Mesa launching a holiday drink menu. Four days before the launch, the owner creates a showcase with a square photo of the new drinks, the headline Holiday drinks are here, a short description and an Order action, set to run for 45 days. The showcase is approved and goes live on launch day.

sections.heading: How this fits your local plan
sections.body_html: Treat this as part of a routine rather than a one-off fix. Local visibility in Anaheim and the rest of Orange County comes from many small, accurate signals adding up: a verified profile, consistent listings, useful service pages, real photos and a flow of honest reviews. Google is open that relevance, distance and popularity drive local results. You cannot change distance, but you can make sure Google and AI assistants understand exactly what you do and see evidence that customers value it. Put a monthly reminder in the calendar to check the profile, read new reviews and update anything that has changed.

sections.heading: What to do this week
sections.body_html:
1. Pick this month's promotion.
  2. Prepare a square photo.
  3. Write a 38-character headline.
  4. Submit at least three days ahead.

sections.heading: When to get help
sections.body_html: You do not need an agency for every step here; Google documents most of it clearly. Consider outside help when the work is urgent and unfamiliar, when you manage several locations, or when the same issue returns after you fix it. Ask any provider to show you the specific guideline or documentation behind each recommendation, to keep you as the owner of your accounts and to report results in calls, bookings and leads rather than vanity numbers. That is how Chimera works with Orange County businesses from our base in Anaheim.

sections.heading: A twelve-month showcase calendar
sections.body_html: Map out a year of showcases in one sitting. January: a new-year offer or service. February: Valentine's Day or a quiet-season promotion. Spring: new menu items, products or spring cleaning services. Summer: longer hours, outdoor seating or summer camps. Fall: back-to-school, Halloween or seasonal menus. November and December: holiday hours, gift cards and events. For each month, note the headline, image and action, then create showcases at least three days before each goes live. Align them with your Google Business Profile posts and newsletter so the same message appears everywhere customers look. For Anaheim businesses near the resort area, add showcases around major conventions and events when visitor numbers rise, and check approval status a few days before each one starts.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Create a monthly showcase with a short headline, a square photo and a clear action, submitted at least three days ahead. Chimera, based in Anaheim, plans showcases and Google posts together for Orange County businesses.

faqs.q: What is an Apple Business showcase?
faqs.a: A module on your Apple Maps place card that promotes offers, events or new items.

faqs.q: How long can a showcase run?
faqs.a: Up to 365 days; the default is 90.
Apple recommends planning at least three calendar days ahead.

faqs.q: How long can the headline be?
Can I use the same showcase for every location?
faqs.a: Yes, or different ones per location.

faqs.q: Can I edit a showcase in review?
faqs.a: You can, but Apple says it may delay approval.

faqs.q: Do you help businesses in Anaheim and Orange County with this?
faqs.a: Yes. Chimera is based in Anaheim, California and works with businesses across Orange County, California.
